title: Luma public calendar sync for Track Record
description:
Track Record should maintain a lightweight AISSA event archive by syncing public Luma calendar events without relying on Luma Plus/API access. AISSA will create public Luma events with registration questions and host approval; the integration should treat guest approval, attendance, and precise hidden location details as Luma-owned data rather than Track Record sync inputs.

The sync should periodically import public event metadata from the Luma calendar iCal feed, enrich records by parsing public Luma event pages for cover/social images, and upsert records into Track Record using stable Luma identifiers. This should support basic event archive coverage while keeping the integration deterministic and non-AI by default.

## Required Skills
vercel:vercel-functions,playwright,beads
design: Use a Vercel Cron-triggered Node.js serverless function to fetch the Luma iCal feed, parse VEVENTs, fetch public event pages for image metadata, and upsert into Track Record. Keep AI out of the core sync path; reserve AI only for later optional enrichment or cleanup. Store source metadata such as externalSource=luma, externalId/UID, lastSeenAt, raw feed timestamps, and image URLs for dedupe and cautious stale detection.
acceptance_criteria: Track Record can periodically sync public Luma calendar events from iCal into the database; synced records dedupe by stable Luma external identifiers; public event pages are parsed for event image URLs where available; hidden/obfuscated location data is handled as best-effort rather than treated as authoritative; the integration does not require Luma API keys, webhooks, Zapier, or Luma Plus; serverless sync state is stored in the database rather than local filesystem.
notes: Context from 2026-05-22 investigation: Luma public calendar feed is http://api2.luma.com/ics/get?entity=calendar&id=cal-p3BboQFpGbi3ioe. The feed returned 59 public/published events while the Luma dashboard showed 107 total events, so missing items are likely private/unlisted. Luma event pages expose images via images.lumacdn.com event-covers/event-social URLs. People stats still require Calendar -> People CSV or a later API/webhook path; this project is only the public event archive sync.
